To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the energy security of Small Island Developing States is affected by seven key dimensions: import dependency; prices; climate change; governance; infrastructure development; equity; and efficiency.

energy security in SICS can be improved by: 1) diversifying the energy mix; 2) reducing import dependence; 3) increasing the use of renewable energy; 4) increasing energy efficiency and energy conservation measures; 5) reducing the use of fossil fuel and 6) reducing the use and production of CO2.
energy security in SICS is shaped by the seven identified dimensions and the key to improving energy security in SICs is to focus on the dimensions that are most relevant to the particular island.
